These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recR9a4OItodWBnvP.Bio: Emily Ridout is a folklorist and AstroYoga specialist who blends astrology, yoga, and tarot; she appeared on InnerVerse (multiple times) to discuss her book AstroYoga for an Aquarian Age.
recR9a4OItodWBnvP.Name: Emily Ridout

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Cancer, the Moon and the Gateway of Man","body":"The night opens on Cancer as the lunar cardinal water sign, the crab that moves sideways, held in tension with Capricorn across the axis of the solstices. The panel walks through what water means as an element of feeling and memory, why the Moon rules reflection rather than radiance, and the old teaching that Cancer marks the gate through which souls descend into bodies while Capricorn marks the way back out. From there the conversation turns to how that gateway quality shows up in plants that soothe, soften and hold."},{"title":"The Chariot Decoded","body":"The tarot section settles on the Chariot, and the reading starts with an oddity: the chariot never moves. Its wheels read as a hub rather than a vehicle, and the canopy overhead becomes a ciborium, the starry firmament stretched above the driver. Krishna appears as the charioteer of the Bhagavad Gita, the Hebrew letter and the sphere of Chesed come in for a look, and Ursa Major turns overhead as the wagon circling the pole. Merkaba mysticism closes the arc, the chariot as a vehicle of ascent rather than travel across ground."},{"title":"Linden and the Willow's Bark","body":"Linden opens the herb walk as a calming, mucilaginous flower for the chest and the lungs, a tree whose blossom tea meets anxiety and grief in the same cup, and which gets named as China's answer to the Bodhi tree, an enlightenment tree in its own right. Willow follows as the original aspirin, salicin in the bark long before the pharmacy, a fever remedy and a lesson in flexibility from a tree that bends rather than breaks. The silvered underside of the leaf, flashing pale when the wind turns it, marks willow as a lunar plant by signature."},{"title":"Marshmallow, Mucilage and Lunaria","body":"Marshmallow root arrives as the cooling, hydrating ally for hot and damp constitutions, slippery with mucilage that coats the gut and the mucous membranes, and the panel traces the true origin of the confection back to the plant that gave it its name. Lunaria follows, the money plant, its translucent seed pods hanging like silver coins or little moons, wrapped in folklore about wealth and about Zeus's cow, another lunar signature hiding in a garden ornamental."},{"title":"Aloe, Coconut and the Tree of Life","body":"Aloe vera enters through Ayurveda as Kumari, the maiden, a plant credited with pacifying all three doshas at once, cooling pitta, moistening vata and moving kapha, fortifying as much as it soothes. Coconut closes the night as the tree of life, fuel for fasting, oil for digestion and for skin and coat, and the center of daily life across Pacific and South Asian cultures. Both plants carry water inside a protective shell, which is about as Cancerian a signature as a plant can offer."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Cancer season herbs and the plants that carry the Moon's signature in flower, bark and sap. Linden, willow, marshmallow, lunaria, aloe and coconut read through the doctrine of signatures, alongside the Chariot card in the tarot and the old teaching that Cancer is the gate souls pass through on the way in.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: This is a remastered edition of a livestream first aired on July 5th, 2023, with the audio cleaned up and the tangents trimmed into a focused session on the lunar cardinal water sign. Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs, Michelle Lundquist, Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies and Emily Ridout join Chance Garton to cover linden tea for anxiety and grief, willow bark as the original aspirin, marshmallow root for the gut and the mucous membranes, lunaria folklore, aloe vera in Ayurvedic medicine, and coconut oil for digestion, skin and fasting.
